title: Responsive presentation CSS must not resurrect semantically suppressed surfaces
summary: A mobile hardsub regression persisted because responsive rules using display:flex/block !important had higher selector specificity than a semantic .hardsub-strategy-suppressed rule. The UI state correctly marked the inactive execution surface as suppressed, but presentation CSS made it visible again. The fix adds stage-aware selectors and a higher-specificity semantic gate keyed by data-media-operation and data-hardsub-strategy. Candidate lesson: semantic visibility state must outrank presentation/layout restoration rules, and regression tests should assert the rendered surface rather than only class presence.

evidence.failing_check: Playwright reported: Parameter-controlled hardsub exposes the goal execution surface on mobile.
evidence.cause: body.ui-mobile .encode-card { display:flex !important } and other mobile presentation rules could override the lower-specificity semantic suppression class.
evidence.relation_to_existing_candidate: Distinct from presentation-regression-isolation-semantic-sync: that candidate concerns test isolation and async semantic completion; this case concerns CSS cascade authority over semantic visibility.
